n-m-h3-dist-02.s.s2.model.0: If first ball white, 2 white balls remain out of 4, so probability na 2/4=1/2. E different from original 3/5, so condition say probability same every time don break, and e no be B(3, 3/5).
n-m-h3-dist-02.s.s2.model.1: If dem no put balls back, result of earlier draw change next probability. If dem draw white first, chance say next one white na 2 out of 4 (0.5), wey different from 3/5; so trials no be independent and e no fit be binomial distribution.

n-m-h3-dist-03.title: Two games with same mean: spread too dey the same?
n-m-h3-dist-03.topic: Probability distributions: variance of sum and multiple of random variables
n-m-h3-dist-03.goal: Compare the distributions directly to decide whether same mean mean same spread too, and explain the reason using variance.
n-m-h3-dist-03.material: Make X the number wey show when dem roll standard six-sided die. Two games dey. For Game A, roll die one time and your score na number wey show times 2 (2X); for Game B, roll am two times and your score na sum of the two numbers (X₁+X₂). Mean score na 7 points for both games. Youngsu talk say, "Since the means dey the same, score spread suppose dey the same too."
n-m-h3-dist-03.thinking.0: Choose comparison method wey test the claim
n-m-h3-dist-03.thinking.1: Build evidence for counterexample using real probabilities
n-m-h3-dist-03.thinking.2: Generalize using rules for how variance change
n-m-h3-dist-03.prereq.0: Expected value and variance of discrete random variable
n-m-h3-dist-03.prereq.1: Variance of sum of two independent random variables V(X+Y)=V(X)+V(Y)
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.prompt: Wetin comparison best fit test Youngsu claim?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.hint.0: Youngsu claim na about "spread," no be mean. Which data go show that?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.hint.1: For each option, think whether e fit show difference between the two games.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.o.a: Calculate again to check say means of the two games really be the same, 7 points
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.r.a: Dem don already tell you say means dey the same. Checking the same value again no go tell you about spread.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.o.b: Use the fact say mean of one die roll na 3.5 to compare the two games
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.r.b: This only tell you say mean of 7 points for both games come from this value. E no show the spread.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.o.c: Put scores wey possible for both games and each score probability side by side
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.r.c: You dey compare the whole score distribution. This fit show directly whether distribution shape fit different even when means dey the same.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.o.d: Roll die many times and see whether average score for both games come near 7 points
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.r.d: This show whether average gather near 7, but e no tell you anything about spread.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s1.explain: Mean na only one summary of distribution. If you put scores and probabilities side by side, you fit see at once whether distribution shape fit different with same mean. Recalculating mean or only checking whether scores gather near mean no fit test Youngsu claim.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.prompt: Find probability say score be 2 or 12 for each game (add the two cases), and explain why Youngsu claim no correct.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.hint.0: Write which die numbers give 2 points and 12 points for Game A.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.hint.1: For Game B, count every ordered pair of two numbers wey give 2 and 12 points, then find how many dem be out of 36 outcomes.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.placeholder: e.g. For Game A, to score 2 points ...
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You count the ways to get 2 and 12 points for Game B as ordered pairs yourself?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You fit say distribution shape fit different even if means dey the same?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You fit explain how difference between the two probabilities show difference for spread?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.model.0: For Game A, roll of 1 or 6 give 2 or 12 points, so na 2/6=1/3. For Game B, only two outcomes dey: (1,1) and (6,6), so na 2/36=1/18. Even though mean same, extreme score probabilities different well well, so spread no fit be the same.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s2.model.1: Probability to score 2 or 12 points na one-third for A and one-eighteenth for B. Even though mean na 7 for both, A dey give extreme scores much more often, so variances different.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.prompt: Make V be variance of number X wey show on one die roll. Wetin be variances of Game A score 2X and Game B score X₁+X₂ (the two rolls no affect each other)?
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.hint.0: 2X na one result doubled, while X₁+X₂ na two different results added. Think about each one separately.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.hint.1: Put simple number for V (for example V=1), find variance for each option, and compare whether dem match spread of the two games from previous step.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.o.a: Variance of 2X na 2V, and variance of X₁+X₂ na 2V
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.r.a: You treat 2X like "X added two times." Adding same value two times different from adding results from two separate rolls.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.o.b: Variance of 2X na 4V, and variance of X₁+X₂ na 2V
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.r.b: For 2X, every value double, so variance become 2² times bigger; for sum of two independent results, variances add, so e become 2 times bigger.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.o.c: Variance of 2X na 4V, and variance of X₁+X₂ na 4V
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.r.c: You apply rule say multiplying by constant make variance multiply by square of the factor to sum of two rolls too. For independent sum, na just add the variances.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.o.d: Variance of 2X na 2V, and variance of X₁+X₂ na 4V
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.r.d: You swap variance of multiple with variance of sum.
n-m-h3-dist-03.s.s3.explain: V(2X)=2²V=4V, and for sum of two independent random variables, V(X₁+X₂)=V+V=2V. The two means na 7, but variances different: 4V and 2V. (Variance of die roll na V=35/12, so dem be 35/3 and 35/6.)

n-m-h3-dist-04.title: Expected value na the value wey show most often?
n-m-h3-dist-04.topic: Probability distributions: meaning of expected value
n-m-h3-dist-04.goal: Sort out definition and meaning of expected value, then build and check distribution where expected value no be possible value and no be the value with highest probability.
n-m-h3-dist-04.material: Random variable X fit take values 0, 1, 2. Once you choose probabilities for the three values for probability distribution table, expected value E(X) dey determined.
n-m-h3-dist-04.thinking.0: Sort statements about expected value into true and false
n-m-h3-dist-04.thinking.1: Build distribution wey meet the conditions and use am as counterexample
n-m-h3-dist-04.prereq.0: Probability distribution table for discrete random variable
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose all correct statements about expected value E(X).
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.hint.0: For each statement, think whether you fit test am by making probability distribution table.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.hint.1: First test am with simple distribution where values na just 0 and 1, with equal probabilities.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.o.a: E(X) na one of the values X fit take
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.r.a: Even if X fit only take integer values, E(X) fit be decimal. For example, mean number of heads for coin toss fit be 0.5.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.o.b: E(X) na sum of each value times its probability.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.o.c: E(X) na value of X wey get highest probability.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.r.c: You treat expected value and "value wey get highest probability" as the same thing. Most likely value na separate idea, and the two usually different.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.o.d: If dem repeat trial many times, mean of observed values gather around E(X).
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.r.d: You correctly describe where the mean settle as dem repeat trial.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s1.explain: E(X) na sum of value × probability, and na value wey mean dey settle around after dem repeat trial plenty times. No guarantee say na value X fit really take, and no guarantee say na value with highest probability.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.prompt: Suppose X fit take values 0, 1, 2. Choose their probabilities as whole-number percentages (p0, p1, p2). Conditions: ① every probability at least 1% and dem sum to 100% ② only value with highest probability na 2 ③ E(X)≤1.2 (expected value at least 0.8 below most likely value 2). Make 3 different examples (different p2 values).
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.hint.0: First choose p0, p1, p2 so dem add to 100, and make p2 the biggest.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.hint.1: Calculate E(X)=(p1+2·p2)/100 and check whether e no pass 1.2. If e too big, try increase p0 or p1.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.hint.2: Change p2 to other values like 45 and 39, then choose p0 and p1 again each time.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Probabilities na whole numbers of at least 1% and dem add up to 100%.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.fail.c1: The 3 probabilities must be whole numbers of at least 1%, and dem must sum to 100.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.ok.c2: Only value 2 get the highest probability.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.fail.c2: P(X=2) must be greater than each of the other two probabilities (e no fit equal either one).
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s2.explain: E(X)=(p1+2·p2)/100. For example, for (40, 15, 45), E(X)=1.05, and value with highest probability na 2. E(X)=1.05 no be value X fit take, and e different from 2, the most likely value. Examples wey only rearrange (p0, p1, p2) no need count as different.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.prompt: Choose one example and use the numbers explain why e wrong to read E(X) as "value wey show most often" or "value wey really show."
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.hint.0: Find E(X) for your example and compare am with values X fit take: 0, 1, 2.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.hint.1: Write how value with highest probability relate to E(X).
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You calculate E(X) yourself for the example you choose?
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You explain why E(X) be value wey no fit really happen?
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You explain how value with highest probability different from E(X)?
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.model.0: For example, for (40, 15, 45), E(X)=0.15 + 0.9 = 1.05. X no fit take this value, and value with highest probability na 2. So E(X) no be the value wey show most often or any value wey fit show.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.model.1: For (37, 24, 39), E(X)=1.02, but X fit only be 0, 1, or 2, so 1.02 no fit happen. Value with highest probability na 2 at 39%, so e different from expected value.
n-m-h3-dist-04.s.s3.model.2: For (25, 36, 39), E(X)=1.14 no be value X fit take, and e different from 2, the most likely value.

n-m-h3-dist-05.goal: Decide whether value fit occur when probability at one point of continuous random variable be 0, explain your judgment, and explain with words wey friend go understand how including or leaving out endpoints affect am.
n-m-h3-dist-05.material: Bus fit arrive at any time from 0 to 10 minutes with equal chance. Waiting time X (minutes) fit be any value from 0 to 10 inclusive. Probability of interval depend on length: P(a≤X≤b)=(b−a)/10. Jia write this:

n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s1.line.2: Since probability na 0, bus arriving exactly after 4 minutes no fit happen.

n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s2.prompt: Write text message to explain to Jia. Say which part of her reasoning need correction, and compare how big P(X≤4) and P(X<4) be, using simple words and example.

But that no mean bus no fit ever arrive after 4 minutes, because e must arrive some time. Whether 4 minutes dey included or not, the probability wey e add na 0, so P(X≤4) and P(X<4) equal.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s2.model.1: Because e continuous, even if one point get probability 0, bus fit still arrive for that moment. E be like one point on line get area 0 even though the line still get points. Adding or removing one point no change probability, so P(X≤4)=P(X<4)=0.4.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s2.model.2: P(X=4)=0, but arrival time na one definite value, so that value no be impossible. One point no get width, so adding or removing am no change probability, and the two probabilities equal.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.hint.0: Think about how each statement depend on value of P(X=a).
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.hint.1: For die roll X (discrete), find P(X≤3) and P(X<3), then compare dem.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.o.a: Even for continuous random variable, P(X≤a) always bigger than P(X<a).
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.r.a: You think say "≤" include more cases, so the probability must be bigger. For continuous random variable, probability at one point na 0, so the two equal.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.o.b: For continuous random variable, if P(X=a)=0, then X no fit equal a.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.r.b: You treat probability 0 as same as impossible. For continuous random variable, value wey get probability 0 fit really happen.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.o.c: For continuous random variable, probability dey the same whether interval endpoints dey included or not.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.r.c: Probability at one point na 0, so including or excluding endpoint no change probability.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.o.d: For discrete random variable too, P(X≤a)=P(X<a) always hold.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.r.d: For discrete random variable, P(X=a) fit be nonzero, so the two no necessarily equal.
n-m-h3-dist-05.s.s3.explain: For continuous random variable, P(X=a)=0, so P(a≤X≤b)=P(a<X<b)=P(a≤X<b)=P(a<X≤b). For discrete random variable, P(X=a)>0 fit happen, so including or leaving out endpoint fit change probability.

n-m-h3-dist-07.s.s1.hint.1: For each option, check whether p you find dey between 0 and 1 and whether n na natural number.

n-m-h3-est-01.title: Checking a solution for probability say 9 bottles average at least 503 mL
n-m-h3-est-01.topic: Statistical estimation: distribution of sample mean
n-m-h3-est-01.goal: Compare mean and standard deviation of sample mean distribution with population values, find and correct wrong line in a solution, and explain why probability for sample mean different from probability for one value.
n-m-h3-est-01.material: For beverage factory, volume of one bottle follow normal distribution with mean 500 mL and standard deviation 6 mL. Haeun, wey work in quality control, randomly pick 9 bottles and find probability say mean volume X̄ at least 503 mL. Part of standard normal table: P(0≤Z≤0.5)=0.1915, P(0≤Z≤1.5)=0.4332, P(0≤Z≤3)=0.4987. (Z na random variable wey follow normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1.)

n-m-h3-est-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose the first wrong line in Haeun solution.

n-m-h3-est-01.s.s1.line.2: Standard deviation of X̄ na 6, same as population standard deviation.
n-m-h3-est-01.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. Standard deviation of sample mean X̄ na population standard deviation divided by square root of sample size: 6/√9=2. So X̄ follow normal distribution with mean 500 and standard deviation 2, and P(X̄≥503)=P(Z≥1.5)=0.5−0.4332=0.0668. Lines 4 and 5 carry the 6 from line 3, so their results wrong (0.3085 na probability say one bottle reach at least 503).
n-m-h3-est-01.s.s2.prompt: Use corrected solution to find P(X̄≥503). Then explain in 1 or 2 sentences how this probability different from probability say one bottle volume at least 503 mL, and why.

n-m-h3-est-01.s.s2.model.0: Standard deviation of sample mean na 6÷√9=2. P(X̄≥503)=P(Z≥1.5)=0.5−0.4332=0.0668. When you average 9 bottles, high and low bottles balance each other, so mean spread less than one bottle, and chance to reach at least 503 much smaller.
n-m-h3-est-01.s.s2.model.1: X̄ follow N(500, 2²), so Z=(503−500)/2=1.5 and probability about 6.68%. For one bottle standard deviation na 6, but for mean e reduce to 2 and gather closer around 500, so chance to reach at least 503 smaller.

n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.prompt: Info show one piece at a time. Each step choose judgment using only what known.
n-m-h3-integc-04.title: Definite integrals without antiderivative
n-m-h3-integc-04.topic: Integration: definite integrals using substitution and interval symmetry (find answer without antiderivative)
n-m-h3-integc-04.goal: As information grow, update your judgment; confirm say symmetry relation from substitution fit determine definite integral without finding antiderivative.
n-m-h3-integc-04.material: Follow each step for finding I=∫_0^{π/2} sin x/(sin x+cos x) dx. (∫_0^{π/2} na definite integral from 0 to π/2.)
n-m-h3-integc-04.thinking.0: Estimate roughly how big answer suppose be
n-m-h3-integc-04.thinking.2: Watch which way interval go after substitution
n-m-h3-integc-04.thinking.3: Judge conditions where same method work
n-m-h3-integc-04.prereq.0: Integration by substitution (change limits in definite integral)
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.hint.0: Every time new information show, count "how many unknowns and how many equations dey."
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether your first estimate and answer you find later dey close.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.info: You want to find I=∫_0^{π/2} sin x/(sin x+cos x) dx. E hard to find antiderivative of this expression directly. Integrand h(x)=sin x/(sin x+cos x) get values h(0)=0, h(π/4)=1/2, h(π/2)=1, and interval length na π/2 (about 1.57).
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.ask: Which estimate for size of I best?
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.after: Height rise from 0 to 1 and middle value na 1/2, so area rough around (1/2)×1.57≈0.8. You fit use this estimate later to check whether answer you find correct.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.o.a: I na about 1.57: because you treat height like 1 and multiply by length 1.57
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Height only reach 1 at end of interval. This estimate treat height as 1 through whole interval.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.o.b: I na about 0.8: because height change from 0 to 1, average about 1/2
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: You estimate height change using average. E no be exact answer, but e fit help measure rough size.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.o.c: I na 0: because h(0)=0 at starting point
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Value be 0 at one point no make definite integral 0. Look at values across whole interval.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.info: Also look at J=∫_0^{π/2} cos x/(sin x+cos x) dx. Add two fractions and numerator become denominator, so I+J=∫_0^{π/2} 1 dx=π/2.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.ask: We fit determine I from this information alone?
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.after: One equation only dey, I+J=π/2, so we no fit find I and J separately. You need one more relation between I and J.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.o.a: We fit determine am: I+J=π/2, so I=π/4.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You split am in half without checking whether I=J. I+J=π/2 na just one relation between I and J.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.o.b: We no fit determine am: I+J=π/2 no help at all to find I.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: The value of I+J na useful information. E give one relation between I and J.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Still no enough: you need one more relation between I and J.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: You notice say two unknowns dey, I and J, but only one equation.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.2.info: For J, let x=π/2−t. Then dx=−dt, and as x move from 0 to π/2, t move from π/2 to 0. Since sin(π/2−t)=cos t and cos(π/2−t)=sin t, J=∫_{π/2}^{0} sin t/(sin t+cos t)·(−dt)=∫_0^{π/2} sin t/(sin t+cos t) dt, wey equal I.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.2.after: I=J and I+J=π/2, so I=π/4 (about 0.785). Dis match first estimate 0.8 well.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: You use both I=J and I+J=π/2 together. E also match first 0.8 estimate.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You mistake I+J for I. J carry same amount too.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: You mistake height at midpoint for definite integral value. Multiply height by interval length too.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s1.reflect: At first, only estimate possible. Even after finding I+J equation, ‘split in half’ too early. Substitution gives J=I, then I determined. Symmetry of interval lets you find integral without antiderivative.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.prompt: When substitute x=π/2−t in J, dx=−dt, but J become +I. Explain by focusing on integration limits.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.hint.0: Find t values corresponding to x=0 and x=π/2; write new lower and upper limits.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.hint.1: When definite integral upper limit below lower limit, how sign change when restore usual order?
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You note after substitution lower limit π/2 and upper 0?
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.model.0: As x move 0 to π/2, t move π/2 to 0, so limits swap. Reversing interval changes sign; together with minus from dx=−dt the signs cancel, so J=+I.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s2.model.1: After substitution interval reverse π/2 to 0. Restoring order adds minus; this and dx minus cancel, making positive.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s3.prompt: Choose integral solvable with same method: replace x with π/2−x and add paired expression.

n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s3.hint.1: Check if numerator and denominator become equal when original and transformed expressions add.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s3.r.a: For interval [0,π/3], x and π/2−x no pair inside same interval, so method no apply directly.
n-m-h3-integc-04.s.s3.r.b: Denominator not symmetric, so paired sum no simplify to constant.

n-m-h3-est-05.s.s1.explain: Sample mean ± 1.96×1.5/√100 = ±0.294. A: 3.106–3.694; B: 2.806–3.394. If you omit √100, such as 3.4±1.96×1.5, interval too wide; z=1.645 gives 90% interval.

n-m-h3-est-05.s.s2.o.d: You no fit judge; with only 100 students for each city, comparison no mean anything.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s2.r.d: Small sample no make interval useless. E still tell you the range where means dey.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s2.explain: The two intervals, 2.806 to 3.394 and 3.106 to 3.694, overlap from 3.106 to 3.394. Overlap na quick check; more exactly, you suppose check whether 95% interval for difference between the two means include 0. Here the difference interval about −0.12 to 0.72, and e include 0, so e hard to conclude say City A longer. But nobody don prove say the two means equal too.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.prompt: Your friend read this article and post for group chat, "City A kids definitely use their phones longer than City B kids." From interval calculations above, write correction message in 2 or 3 sentences, using words wey high school friend go understand.

n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.hint.1: Then explain simply wetin possibility the interval overlap still leave open.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.placeholder: e.g. The article talk 3.4 hours and 3.1 hours, but ...

n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You mention interval overlap as evidence at least once?
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You stay balanced by saying "hard to know for sure" instead of "wrong"?
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.model.0: Just because A get 3.4 hours and B get 3.1, e too early to say A longer. Dem survey only 100 students each, and the 95% confidence intervals, about 3.11 to 3.69 for A and about 2.81 to 3.39 for B, overlap. In reality, the two cities fit be about the same.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.model.1: The 0.3-hour difference between sample means dey within margin of error. Since the two confidence intervals overlap, e hard to say A students use theirs longer, and the two fit be equal.
n-m-h3-est-05.s.s3.model.2: The difference na only 0.3 hours, so dem fit be similar and I no fit say for sure. The two intervals overlap.

n-m-h3-integc-02.title: Making different cubic functions with definite integral 4
n-m-h3-integc-02.topic: Integration: properties of definite integrals — cancellation of odd-power terms on symmetric interval
n-m-h3-integc-02.goal: Use fact say definite integrals of odd-power terms on symmetric interval equal 0 to build different functions with same definite integral, and explain the structure.
n-m-h3-integc-02.material: Think about definite integral of cubic function f(x)=ax³+bx²+cx+d over [−1,1]. (x³ mean x cubed, and ∫_{-1}^{1} na definite integral from −1 to 1.)

n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s1.prompt: Choose all functions wey definite integral over [−1,1] equal 0.

n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s1.r.a: Even-degree terms get same value at x and −x, so dem no cancel. Calculate definite integral of each of the two terms.
n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s1.r.b: You notice say only odd-degree terms dey, so values at x and −x opposite.
n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s1.r.e: You notice say only odd-degree terms dey, so values at x and −x opposite.

n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s1.explain: For terms wey get opposite values at x and −x (x, x³, x⁵, …), area for left and right over [−1,1] only differ by sign, so definite integral 0. For x⁴−x², e be 2/5−2/3; for x³+1, e be 2; for x²+x, e be 2/3; none equal 0.
n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s2.prompt: Make f(x)=ax³+bx²+cx+d (a, b, c, d integers from −20 to 20 inclusive), with ∫_{-1}^{1} f(x)dx = 4. Make 3 different f where x³ and x terms really dey (a≠0, c≠0). Enter a, b, c, d for each.

n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s2.fail.c2: If a be 0, x³ term no dey.
n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s2.fail.c3: If c be 0, x term no dey.
n-m-h3-integc-02.s.s2.explain: Over [−1,1], ∫ax³dx=0 and ∫cx dx=0, so ∫f(x)dx = 2b/3 + 2d. If e equal 4, then b+3d=6. Examples na (1,0,2,2), (3,3,−1,1), and (−2,6,5,0). (1,3,2,2) give 2+4=6, no be 4; and examples with a=0 or c=0 no meet conditions.

n-m-h3-integc-03.title: Volume from rotating region between two curves: where mistake happen?
n-m-h3-integc-03.topic: Integration: volume of solid from rotating region between two curves (shape of cross-section)
n-m-h3-integc-03.goal: For solution to volume of solid wey come from rotating region between two curves, find and correct line wey get cross-section shape wrong, and identify which region volume wrong expression actually give.
n-m-h3-integc-03.material: Soyoung find volume of solid wey dem get by rotating region between curves y=x and y=x² one time around x-axis. (x² mean x squared.)
n-m-h3-integc-03.thinking.0: Draw shape of cross-section at one point
n-m-h3-integc-03.thinking.1: Work backward to find region the wrong expression represent
n-m-h3-integc-03.thinking.2: Confirm mistake by directly comparing cross-section areas
n-m-h3-integc-03.prereq.0: Volume of solid wey rotate around x-axis
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.prompt: Choose first wrong line in Soyoung solution.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.hint.0: Choose one point like x=1/2 and sketch how far region dey from x-axis there and how wide e extend.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.hint.1: Decide whether rotated cross-section na solid disk or disk with hole.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.line.0: Curves y=x and y=x² meet at x=0 and x=1, and on 0≤x≤1, x≥x².
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.line.1: When dem rotate this region around x-axis, cross-section at x na circle with radius x−x².
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.line.2: So volume na V = π∫_0^1 (x−x²)² dx.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s1.explain: Line 2 first wrong. When region between two curves rotate around x-axis, cross-section na washer, disk with hole (outer radius x, inner radius x²). E no be circle with radius equal to difference between two radii. From line 3, calculation follow the wrong cross-section from line 2, so arithmetic right but result wrong.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.prompt: Correct the wrong line and find volume. Then use cross-section at x=1/2 to explain in 1 or 2 sentences why Soyoung expression no correct.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.hint.0: Sketch cross-section at x to check whether e be big circle radius x with small circle radius x² removed.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.hint.1: At x=1/2, write and compare area of big circle, small circle, and Soyoung circle.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You write outer and inner radius for cross-section at x and find area?
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You compare Soyoung cross-section area with correct one at x=1/2?
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.selfAssess.2: You notice say (x−x²)² and x²−x⁴ different?
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.model.0: Cross-section at x na washer with outer radius x and inner radius x², so area na π(x²−x⁴). V=π∫_0^1 (x²−x⁴)dx=π(1/3−1/5)=2π/15. At x=1/2 correct cross-section na π(1/4−1/16)=3π/16, but Soyoung expression give circle radius 1/4, with area only π/16.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s2.model.1: Cross-section wey come from rotating region between two curves na big disk minus small disk, so e be π(x²)−π(x²)², and volume 2π/15. Squaring difference of radii no be the same as difference between areas of big and small circles.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.prompt: Soyoung expression π∫_0^1 (x−x²)² dx na volume of which region dem rotate once around x-axis?

n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.hint.1: For each option, write shape of cross-section at x after rotation around x-axis.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.o.a: Region wey y=x and y=x² enclose
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.r.a: This region give cross-section with hole, so you suppose integrate π(x²−x⁴). Check cross-section at x=1/2.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.o.b: Region wey y=x, x-axis, and x=1 enclose
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.r.b: Cross-section for this region na solid circle radius x, so e become π∫x²dx.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.o.c: Region wey y=x², x-axis, and x=1 enclose
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.r.c: Cross-section for this region na solid circle radius x², so e become π∫x⁴dx.
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.o.d: Region wey y=x−x² and x-axis enclose
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.r.d: You notice this na region wey give solid circles with radius equal to curve height x−x².
n-m-h3-integc-03.s.s3.explain: y=x−x² dey at least 0 on 0≤x≤1, and when region between this curve and x-axis rotate around x-axis, cross-section na solid circle with radius x−x². Soyoung expression give volume for this region (π/30), while volume for region in question (between two curves) na 2π/15.

n-m-h3-integc-05.title: Definite integrals of periodic functions: what info needed?
n-m-h3-integc-05.topic: Integration: definite integral rules, periodic function integrals and info selection
n-m-h3-integc-05.goal: For periodic integral, separate needed period and one-period integral from unneeded facts; key is interval length multiple of period.
n-m-h3-integc-05.material: Continuous function f; find definite integral ∫_2^{11} f(x)dx. (∫_2^{11} means definite integral from 2 to 11.)
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.prompt: f continuous on all reals. Choose all info below absolutely needed to determine ∫_2^{11} f. (Don't select unnecessary.)
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.hint.0: Find interval [2,11] length, divide by 3 and see.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.hint.1: Remove each info one by one; check whether answer still fixed.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.r.a: [0,2] no overlap [2,11]. Think how this value would help find the value on [2,11].
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.r.b: This says same shape repeat every 3 units, linking separate intervals.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.r.c: Even only means left-right symmetry around 0; not used to divide [2,11] into repeating periods.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.r.d: You realize need one-period definite integral to determine whole value.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.r.e: Function value at one point no affect definite integral.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s1.explain: Length [2,11] na 9, which equals 3 periods of length 3. Any period integral same, so ∫_2^{11}f=3×6=18. Need periodicity and one-period integral only.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.prompt: Using period 3 and ∫_0^3f=6, give two intervals [p,q] with determinable integral. p,q integers, p not multiple 3, 0<p, 4≤q−p≤20, q≤40.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.hint.0: First, periodicity: what integral over [1,4] length 3?
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.hint.1: Choose p,q so interval length divided by 3 whole number; ensure p not multiple 3.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.ok.c1: p and q integers inside range.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.fail.c3: q−p length not between 4 and 20 inclusive.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.fail.c4: Interval length no multiple of 3, so value unknown.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.explain: If length multiple of 3, it is whole periods joined, so any start gives (length/3)×6. (1,7) gives 6, (2,11) gives 18, (4,19) gives 30. (1,8) length 7, not multiple 3, unknown; (3,9) excluded because p multiple 3; (1,4) length 3, below 4.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.prompt: Explain why value fixed even if start p no multiple of 3.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.hint.0: Split [p,q] into length-3 intervals. How many parts?
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.hint.1: By periodicity, what integrals over [1,4] and [2,5], each length 3?
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.placeholder: e.g. If interval length multiple of 3 ...
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You verify length-3 interval integral 6 even if p not multiple 3?
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You say length 9 splits into 3 period intervals?
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.model.0: If length multiple of 3, split into periods. Any start point gives each period integral 6, so total (length/3)×6.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s2.because.model.1: If q−p multiple of 3, [p,q] is length-3 pieces; every length-3 interval integral 6 regardless start, so p no need multiple 3.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.prompt: Same info (period 3, ∫_0^3f=6). Choose true statement about ∫_2^{10}f.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.hint.0: Split [2,10] into length-3 pieces and find leftover length.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.hint.1: Compare different f satisfying period 3 and ∫_0^3f=6 (constant f=2 and another).
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.o.a: Determined: average height per period 2, so length 8 integral 16
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.r.a: If interval no split into full periods, average no enough. It has 2.67 periods.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.o.b: Determined: two periods give 12, leftover counted as 0
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.r.b: There is no reason integral on leftover length 2 should equal 0.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.o.c: Not determined: leftover length-2 integral unknown after two periods.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.r.c: You notice length 8 no multiple of 3, so not exact periods.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.o.d: Not determined because start 2 no multiple 3
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.r.d: Start being multiple 3 no matter. Recall previous check.
n-m-h3-integc-05.s.s3.explain: [2,10] length 8: two full periods (length 6) plus leftover length 2. Leftover integral unknown. f=2 gives 16; f=2+cos(2πx/3) gives about 16.83. Both period 3 and ∫_0^3f=6. Start point multiple 3 irrelevant.

n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.ok.c1: p and q integers inside range.
n-m-h3-integc-07.title: If integral smaller, is function smaller everywhere?
n-m-h3-integc-07.goal: Make counterexample showing comparison property only one direction; decide what converse can guarantee (existence).
n-m-h3-integc-07.material: Minsu reason about f,g on 0≤x≤2. (∫_0^2 means integral 0 to 2.)
n-m-h3-integc-07.thinking.2: Use contrapositive to identify sure conclusion
n-m-h3-integc-07.prereq.1: Integrals of linear and constant functions
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.prompt: Choose first logic error in Minsu argument.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.hint.0: In lines 1 and 2, find the assumption and conclusion in each, then check if swapped.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.hint.1: Does line 3 prove line 2 always true or show only one example?
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.line.1: Conversely, if ∫_0^2 f(x)dx < ∫_0^2 g(x)dx, then f(x)<g(x) for every x in 0≤x≤2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.line.2: For example, f(x)=x,g(x)=3: ∫_0^2 f(x)dx=2 < 6=∫_0^2g(x)dx, and f(x)<g(x) on 0≤x≤2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s1.explain: Line 2 wrong. Definite-integral comparison only goes one way: if f≤g for each x, integral f≤integral g. Converse no generally hold. Line 3 only show one example where true; no prove line 2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.prompt: Show with examples why Minsu line 2 wrong. Let f(x)=px and g(x)=q (p,q integers from 1 to 30). Find 3 pairs where ∫_0^2f(x)dx<∫_0^2g(x)dx but some x with 0≤x≤2 has f(x)>g(x).
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.hint.0: Write ∫_0^2 px dx and ∫_0^2 q dx using p,q; make comparison condition.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.hint.1: f=px increases as x grows. Compare f(2) and g(2) at endpoint x=2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.fail.c1: p and q must be integers from 1 to 30 inclusive.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.ok.c3: At x=2, f(2)=2p bigger than g(2)=q.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.fail.c3: No x dey for 0≤x≤2 where f(x)>g(x).
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.explain: ∫_0^2 px dx = 2p and ∫_0^2 q dx = 2q. 2p<2q mean p<q, and for f(2)=2p bigger than g(2)=q at x=2, q<2p need to hold. So examples with p<q<2p, like (3,4), (5,7), and (10,11), na counterexamples. (3,6) get q=2p, so f(2)=g(2) and f(x)≤g(x) hold everywhere, so e no be counterexample.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.prompt: Choose one (p, q) you enter, and give one x value where f(x)>g(x) plus the two definite integral values, to explain why e counterexample to Minsu line 2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.hint.0: Choose one x where f(x)>g(x), and write values of f and g there.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.hint.1: Calculate both definite integral values and compare which one bigger.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: You confirm with actual numbers one x where f(x)>g(x)?
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You calculate both definite integral values and check the inequality?
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.model.0: If (p, q)=(3,4), then ∫_0^2 3x dx=6 and ∫_0^2 4 dx=8, so ∫f<∫g. But at x=2, f(2)=6 and g(2)=4, so f(2)>g(2). Integral of f smaller, but at some x f bigger, so na counterexample to line 2.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s2.because.model.1: For (5,7), definite integrals na 10 and 14, so f integral smaller. But at x=2, f(2)=10 bigger than g(2)=7. So even if integral smaller, function no be smaller at every x.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.prompt: Suppose ∫_0^2 f(x)dx < ∫_0^2 g(x)dx dey true. Wetin you fit say for sure under this condition?
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.hint.0: Write what comparison between definite integrals suppose happen if you assume "f≥g at every x."
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.hint.1: Think what conclusion still hold if that result clash with condition wey dem give.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.o.a: At least one x dey in interval where f(x)<g(x).
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.r.a: You use contrapositive of property say if f≥g for every x, integral f must be at least integral g.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.r.b: You no fit determine value at one point x=1 from definite-integral comparison. You fit build example where f bigger at x=1 too.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.r.c: Counterexample wey you make earlier break this claim. Even if integral smaller, f fit be bigger at some x.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.o.d: No x dey in interval where f(x)>g(x).
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.r.d: For counterexample, f(2)>g(2) at x=2. Some points fit get f bigger.
n-m-h3-integc-07.s.s3.explain: If f(x)≥g(x) at every x, then ∫f ≥ ∫g must hold. The condition ∫f<∫g contradict that, so at least one x get f(x)<g(x). But you no fit know where that x dey, how many dem dey, or whether any x get f>g.

n-m-h3-integc-06.title: Integration by parts: can u be chosen any way?
n-m-h3-integc-06.topic: Integration: choosing u and v′ in parts
n-m-h3-integc-06.goal: Confirm remaining integral difficulty depends on choice of u,v′, and explain simple choosing rules to friend.
n-m-h3-integc-06.material: Hajun integrate ∫xeˣdx by parts using u=eˣ, v′=x, making expression harder. Hajun ask, ‘Can’t choose u and v′ any way?’ (eˣ means e power x; ln x natural log.)
n-m-h3-integc-06.thinking.0: Compare remaining integral under different choices
n-m-h3-integc-06.thinking.1: Set choosing rule (simpler after differentiating / easy to integrate)
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.prompt: Hajun use u=eˣ, v′=x for ∫xeˣdx. Which describes result?
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.hint.0: With u=eˣ, v′=x, find u′ and v, then write RHS uv−∫u′v dx.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.hint.1: Compare original and remaining integral: how x power change?
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.o.a: Remaining integral has x², so power rise
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.r.a: You see swapping u,v′ makes integrating v′ raise power, making remaining integral harder.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.o.b: Remaining integral becomes 0, so answer immediate
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.r.b: For remaining integral 0, u′v must 0. Find u′ and v to check.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.o.c: Parts formula no hold, so impossible
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.r.c: Formula hold regardless of u choice. Remaining integral difficulty changes.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.r.d: Remaining is u′=eˣ times v=x²/2. Find them.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s1.explain: u=eˣ,v′=x give u′=eˣ,v=x²/2, so ∫xeˣdx=(x²/2)eˣ−∫(x²/2)eˣdx. Remaining x power one higher, harder. Formula valid but poor choice. If u=x,v′=eˣ, remaining just ∫eˣdx.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.prompt: For ∫x ln x dx with parts, choose best advice for Hajun.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.hint.0: For each choice, first check if v easy to find.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.hint.1: Compare whether u′v product simpler than original integral.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.r.a: Finding v from ln x not immediate (xlnx−x). Remaining integral still has ln x, no simpler.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.o.b: Best choose u=1, v′=x ln x
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.r.b: Antiderivative xlnx is same original problem; no progress.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.r.c: You choose ln x (simpler when differentiated) as u and x (easy integrate) as v′.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.o.d: Choice no matter; remaining always same difficulty
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.r.d: Choice can make remaining integral easier or harder. Recall earlier example.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s2.explain: u=ln x, v′=x: u′=1/x, v=x²/2, so ∫xlnx dx=(x²/2)lnx−∫(x/2)dx=(x²/2)lnx−x²/4+C. Remaining integral linear and simple. Choose factor simpler after derivative as u; easy to integrate as v′. When y differentiate ln x, e turn 1/x.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.prompt: Reply to Hajun's ‘Can choose u,v′ any way?’ Use ∫xlnx dx to explain in simple words good choice and why.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.hint.0: For ∫xlnx dx, which of ln x and x simpler to differentiate, and which easy integrate?
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.hint.1: Write remaining integral with choice and use as evidence.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You state one-sentence choosing rule, no ‘any way’?
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You write in words Hajun understands, not just symbols?
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.model.0: Hajun, formula works any choice, but remaining integral may get easier or harder. For ∫xlnx dx use u=lnx,v′=x: ln x become 1/x when differentiated and x easy integrate; remaining ∫x/2 dx simple.
n-m-h3-integc-06.s.s3.model.1: Try u=lnx,v′=x: choose factor becoming simpler by differentiation as u, easy-integrate factor as v′. Remaining x/2 solved quickly. If u=x, integrating ln x first harder.

n-m-h3-prob-03.title: Which study app work better?
n-m-h3-prob-03.topic: Probability: conditional probability, independence/dependence, Bayesian reasoning, setting up sample space
n-m-h3-prob-03.goal: Check say overall rates and rates inside each group fit point opposite ways, updating your judgment each time more data show.
n-m-h3-prob-03.material: You want to compare "percentage of students whose grades improve" among students at one school who use study app A or app B. Numbers dey come out one step at a time.

n-m-h3-prob-05.title: Five heads in a row: tails due now?
n-m-h3-prob-05.goal: Spot the wrong idea about probability after a run of results, then say the same thing in a way younger secondary-school sibling fit understand.
n-m-h3-prob-05.material: Your younger sibling dey toss fair coin and talk, "Heads show 5 times in a row! No be time for tails now?" Coin fair: heads and tails get same chance. Your sibling dey 7th grade.
n-m-h3-prob-05.thinking.1: Choose explanation wey suit the person
n-m-h3-prob-05.thinking.2: Explain am yourself with simple words
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.prompt: You toss fair coin and heads show 5 times in a row. Which statement about chance of heads on sixth toss correct?
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.hint.0: Think whether coin remember previous tosses or try balance dem out.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.hint.1: Compare wetin we dey predict for "when we no know first 5 tosses" and "after first 5 heads don already happen."
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.o.a: This coin dey land heads often, so chance of heads bigger than 1/2.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.r.a: Even though coin fair, you think earlier results change the coin kind.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.o.b: Heads don show plenty, so na tails turn now, and chance of heads below 1/2.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.r.b: You think earlier results must be "balanced out." Coin no remember old tosses and adjust to match dem.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.o.c: No matter wetin happen for first 5 tosses, chance of heads on sixth toss stay 1/2.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.o.d: Chance of 6 heads in a row na 1/64, so chance of heads on sixth toss too na 1/64.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.r.d: You mix up chance of predicting all 6 tosses from the start with chance of predicting one toss after first 5 already happen.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s1.explain: Each fair-coin toss independent, so even if we know earlier results, chance of heads on sixth toss na 1/2. Probability 1/64 for 6 heads in a row na value for predicting all six before tossing; with condition say first 5 heads don already happen, e be (1/64)÷(1/32)=1/2.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.prompt: You want to explain to your 7th-grade sibling "why sixth toss still 50-50 heads or tails." Choose most suitable explanation.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.hint.0: For each explanation, write one line wetin your sibling fit ask next.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.hint.1: Check separately whether content correct and whether your sibling fit read and understand am.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.o.a: Since events independent, P(H6 | H1~H5) = P(H6) = 1/2.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.r.a: Plenty symbols and terms dey, so your sibling go hard to follow. E miss step of saying same content in everyday words.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.o.b: Coin no fit remember earlier results. You toss am fresh every time, so sixth toss still 50-50 heads or tails.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.o.c: If you toss enough times, eventually e balance to 50-50, so this time tails a little more likely.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.r.c: You read "eventually e balance" like next toss go make up for heads. E actually support wrong idea.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.o.d: Five in a row really amazing. If sixth one too heads, you suppose suspect the coin.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.r.d: This ignore condition say coin fair. This explanation no answer your sibling misconception.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s2.explain: Good explanation say the same content using words sibling know. B explain independence simply with "e no remember" and "you toss am fresh every time"; A correct but symbols hard; C support wrong idea; D ignore coin fair condition.
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s3.prompt: Your sibling ask, "But chance of 6 heads in a row na only 1/64. If sixth too heads, that really rare!" Answer with simple words your sibling fit understand. (Try no use symbols or terms like P( ) or "conditional.")

n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s3.placeholder: e.g. 1/64 na ... First five tosses don already ...

n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You say chance now, with only sixth toss left, na 1/2?
n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You explain using only words your sibling know?

n-m-h3-prob-05.s.s3.model.1: First five tosses don finish, and coin no remember dem. So sixth toss heads or tails get same 1/2 chance. 1/64 na chance of getting all six right from before, so e different from the situation now.

n-m-h3-prob-07.topic: Probability: conditional probability, independence/dependence, Bayesian reasoning, setting up sample space
n-m-h3-prob-07.title: The First Ball We Never See: Wetin Be the Probability for the Second Ball?
n-m-h3-prob-07.goal: Check how probability dey change when condition change as dem dey reveal information one step after another, and understand say information we learn later fit change probability of an earlier draw too.
n-m-h3-prob-07.material: Do the activity below with balls inside bag. Once person draw one ball, dem no put am back, and every ball get the same chance to come out.
n-m-h3-prob-07.thinking.0: Split the unknown cases and join the results
n-m-h3-prob-07.thinking.1: Use wetin we learn take narrow the sample space
n-m-h3-prob-07.thinking.2: Know difference between time order and where information dey point
n-m-h3-prob-07.prereq.0: Product of probabilities when dem draw without replacement
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.prompt: Dem dey reveal information one by one. For each stage, choose probability using only wetin you know by then.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.hint.0: For each stage, check if you learn anything new and whether e change the balls wey remain.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.hint.1: If one ball color no clear to you, split am into cases by color and add the probabilities of the cases.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.info: One dark bag get 3 red balls and 5 blue balls (all the same shape). Mina remove one ball and hide am for one side without checking the color. Then she remove one more ball from the bag.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.ask: Wetin be the probability say the second ball wey dem remove na red?
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.after: If probability say the hidden ball na red be 3/8, then red probability among the remaining balls na 2/7; if probability say e blue na 5/8, then remaining red probability na 3/7. So (3/8)(2/7)+(5/8)(3/7)=21/56=3/8. If we no know the first ball, probability for the second ball color na the same as the original proportion.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.o.a: 3/7: calculate as if the hidden ball na blue
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.r.a: You calculate as if the hidden ball color don set as blue. Right now we no know that color.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.o.b: 3/8: split into cases by the hidden ball color and add am; e give the same as the original proportion
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.o.c: 2/7: calculate as if the hidden ball na red
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You calculate as if the hidden ball color don set as red. Right now we no know that color.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.o.d: No fit determine: because we no know the hidden ball color
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.0.r.d: You no use the method of splitting into cases and joining dem. Even if we no know the color, we fit find am if we know the probability of each case.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.info: Mina open the ball wey she hide, and na red ball. (Dem never check the second ball.)
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now, wetin be the probability say the second ball wey dem remove na red?
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.after: Now we know say the hidden ball na red; the balls wey remain na 2 red and 5 blue, 7 altogether. So probability say the second ball na red drop reach 2/7.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.o.a: 3/7: 3 red balls dey among the 7 wey remain
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You know say the hidden ball na red but you no adjust the number of red balls wey reduce.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.o.b: 3/8: the original proportion still dey the same
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You no use the information from checking the hidden ball. When information increase, the makeup of the remaining balls dey change.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.1.o.c: 2/7: 2 red balls dey among the 7 wey remain
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.info: Another day, you do am again with the same bag. This time, while the first ball still dey hidden, you open the second ball wey you remove next, and na red ball. Dem never check the first ball.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.ask: Wetin be the probability say the first ball, wey you hide earlier, na red?
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.after: P(first red | second red) = P(both red)÷P(second red) = (3/8×2/7)÷(3/8) = 2/7. Knowing say the second ball na red, we calculate as if one red ball don comot, so probability say the first ball na red too drop from 3/8 reach 2/7.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.o.a: 2/7: if we know say second ball na red, probability say first ball na red dey reduce
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.o.b: 3/8: dem don draw the first ball already, so knowing about second one no dey change am
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You mix time order with where the information dey point. Information we learn later fit change probability of an earlier result too.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.o.c: 5/7: the second ball na red, so the first one likely na blue
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.st.2.r.c: The question ask probability say the first ball na red, but you give probability say e blue. Check if the two values add up to 1.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s1.reflect: Before we see any ball, probability for the second ball na 3/8, same as the beginning; but once we know the first ball, e change reach 2/7. Also, learning about the ball dem draw later change probability for the one dem draw earlier. Conditional probability depend no be on time order, but on "wetin we know."
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.prompt: Explain to your friend why probability say the second ball, wey dem remove without knowing the first ball color, na red be 3/8. (Na the friend wey talk say e no fit calculate if you no know the first ball color.)
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.hint.0: Write the case where the hidden ball na red and the case where e blue separately, then find probability say the second ball na red for each case.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.hint.1: Multiply by the probability of each case, add the two cases, and calculate wetin come out.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.placeholder: For example, when the hidden ball na red and when e blue, ...
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.selfAssess.0: You split am into cases by the first ball color, or give reason say both colors get the same chance?
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.selfAssess.1: You write the steps to multiply and add the case probabilities to get 3/8?
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.model.0: If the hidden ball na red, red probability for the remaining balls na 2/7; if e blue, e na 3/7. So multiply dem by their probabilities 3/8 and 5/8 and add: (3/8)(2/7)+(5/8)(3/7)=3/8.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.model.1: If we no know the first ball, any of the 8 balls get the same chance to be the second one wey dem remove, so probability say e red na the original proportion, 3/8.
n-m-h3-prob-07.s.s2.model.2: If hidden ball na red, red probability for the remaining balls na 2/7; if e blue, e na 3/7. So 3/8×2/7+5/8×3/7=3/8.

n-m-h3-serieslim-03.material: Square R1 get side length 8. Join midpoints of its sides to make square R2; join midpoints of R2 sides to make R3, and continue forever. To find total areas and total perimeters of R1, R2, R3, …, Jiwon send friend message below.

n-m-h3-vec-06.title: Explain Dot Product to Younger Sibling Wey Never Learn Cosine
n-m-h3-vec-06.goal: Explain wetin dot product mean (one number wey show how much two vectors dey point the same way) to person wey no know cosine, by changing the situation.
n-m-h3-vec-06.material: Jisu explain dot product of vectors to her younger sibling for JSS 1 like this: "Dot product of vectors a and b na |a||b|cosθ. You just multiply their parts and add, and e na 0 if dem perpendicular." Her sibling never learn cos yet, so e ask, "But wetin be dot product?" (|a| na size, θ dem read as "theta," and cos na cosine.) 7

n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.o.a: Dot product na one number wey show how much one vector dey point the same way as the other, while considering their sizes.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.r.a: This explanation catch all dot product properties: e bigger when directions agree more, e na 0 when perpendicular, and negative when dem point opposite ways.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.o.b: Dot product na calculation wey multiply the parts of two vectors together to make new vector. The result na arrow too.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.r.b: Dot product result no be vector, na one number. You mix how dem calculate am with the kind of result.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.o.c: Dot product na product of the two vector sizes. E give same value whichever way the two arrows point.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.r.c: Dot product value depend on angle between two vectors. This explanation no consider direction.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.o.d: Dot product na value wey tell angle between two vectors in degrees. If dem form right angle, you get 90.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.r.d: Dot product no be the angle itself. When angle na right angle, dot product na 0, no be 90.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s1.explain: Dot product na one number wey depend on both sizes of vectors and angle between dem. E grow when directions resemble more, na 0 when perpendicular, and negative when dem point opposite ways. A mistake result for vector, B no consider direction, and D mix am up with angle itself.

If rope slant, na part of force dey help; if you pull straight up, none dey move am forward, so e na 0. Dot product na one number wey show how much force dey help in direction of movement.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s2.model.1: When you push cart, e move best when you push the same way e dey face. If direction small off, e help less; if you push sideways at right angle, e no help am move forward, so na 0. Dot product na number wey show how much two arrows dey point the same way.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s2.model.2: If you pull rope upward, none of am dey help move forward, so na 0. If e point exactly where sled dey go, all the force dey help.
n-m-h3-vec-06.s.s2.model.3: If you pull straight where sled dey go, all force dey help; if e slant, na part dey help. At right angle, e na 0.

n-m-h3-vec-07.title: If No Two Planes Parallel, Must Three Planes Meet at One Point?
n-m-h3-vec-07.goal: Test prediction about where three planes dey with counterexample you make yourself, and explain the structure of that example.
n-m-h3-vec-07.material: Think about three different planes. One friend talk say if no two planes parallel, all three must meet for one point. Two planes x=0 and y=0 no parallel, and dem meet along one line. (Dem read x=0 as "x equals 0," and ax+by+cz=d na equation of plane.)
n-m-h3-vec-07.thinking.0: Test prediction with examples you make

n-m-h3-vec-07.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think of wetin your friend talk?

n-m-h3-vec-07.s.s1.o.b: E always true. Planes wey no parallel must meet, so three planes too meet for one point
n-m-h3-vec-07.s.s1.r.b: Two planes meeting pair by pair and three planes having one point in common na different things.

n-m-h3-vec-07.s.s2.prompt: Planes x=0 and y=0 dey. Choose third plane ax+by+cz=d so no two planes parallel and all three get no common point. a,b,c,d na real numbers. Make three different planes.

Put point (0, 0, z) on z-axis inside and get cz=d; for no z to satisfy this, we need c=0 and d≠0. Also a and b must not be 0, so plane no parallel to x=0 or y=0.
